title: A SAT Scalpel for Lattice Surgery: Representation and Synthesis of Subroutines for Surface-Code Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computing
problem: Lattice-surgery subroutines used in surface-code fault-tolerant quantum computing are manually designed with suboptimal spacetime volume. The challenge is to systematically explore and synthesize optimal designs for these frequently-used quantum error correction components.
motivation: Minimizing spacetime volume of lattice-surgery subroutines is critical for reducing the overall overhead of fault-tolerant quantum computing.
method: LaSsynth formalizes lattice-surgery subroutine design by defining variables and constraints that represent the construction problem. It encodes this formulation into SAT (Boolean satisfiability) instances and queries SAT solvers for solutions. The tool iteratively invokes the solver with progressively shrinking spacetime volume bounds to derive increasingly compact designs, enabling exhaustive design-space exploration.
key_novelty: Representing lattice-surgery subroutine design as a SAT problem to enable provably optimal circuit synthesis through exhaustive solver-based exploration.
contributions: Formal representation of lattice-surgery subroutines with variables and constraints suitable for SAT encoding
LaSsynth synthesizer that encodes construction problems as SAT instances for automated optimization
Iterative refinement method with shrinking spacetime volume constraints to discover optimal designs
Demonstration of 8-18% spacetime volume reduction compared to state-of-the-art human designs for T-factories

metrics.other: 8% and 18% spacetime volume reduction versus state-of-the-art designs

primary_theme: SAT-based quantum circuit synthesis for error correction
